notes: On the specific question posed: the three named Stratus threads ($85K/$102K/$91K three-plant-plus-Terre-Haute diagnostic in e60f18c2e4b60006, and the $95K-to-$76K four-DC diagnostic in e20f18c2e4b60019) are genuinely distinct engagements — they name non-overlapping facilities (Rockford/Peoria/Gary/Terre Haute vs. Denver/Columbus/Allentown/Reno), run on separate timelines, and were never conflated in the gold item text, so curator's decision not to merge them is correct. But the mailbox has more Stratus proposal traffic than the curator_notes account for: a third proposal (line-balancing across 'two Ohio lines,' priced $148K-168K in e10f18c2e4b60009, still 'finishing internally' per e10f18c2e4b60007 as of Jul 29 2:10pm) and a fourth (a 'distribution network redesign' phase-1 priced $210,000 in the Jul 23 Zoom-recording summary e40f18c2e4b60024). The '$340K recap' the curator dismisses in one line is not merely an internal aside — it originates in a real, SENT-to-Owen commitment email (e50f18c2e4b60034, Jul 29 8:50am) promising a signed SOW by Aug 1 and a kickoff the week of Aug 10, and is reaffirmed twice more (Aug 5 to Gordon, Aug 11 to Ana). That Jul 29 8:50am email directly contradicts a same-day 2:10pm email in a different thread saying the pricing is still being finalized internally and won't reach Owen as a full proposal until Aug 3 — i.e., the corpus itself, not just the curator's scoping choice, is internally inconsistent about what Stratus deal is actually landed and when. Combined with the Aug 11 same-day contradiction described in the second finding above, my conclusion is that this is a genuine corpus inconsistency around the Stratus relationship's dollar figures and status, not merely five cleanly-distinct parallel engagements — and the gold set's treatment (silently including only the cleanest of the threads, item 01, and saying nothing about the others) under-reports that mess rather than resolving or flagging it. Given the scale of the ambiguity, I did not attempt to add items for the Ohio-lines or network-redesign threads myself (their own internal evidence is too self-contradictory to state a confident current_value), but a human curator should decide whether to (a) exclude Stratus dollar figures from Q5 entirely pending corpus cleanup, or (b) add an explicit must_not_include / notes entry warning that '$340K' and 'the Stratus diagnostic is signing at ~$90-91K' cannot both be treated as current.
